LESSON: SELF- AWARENESS IN THE COMMUNITY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Life Skills in Education
Topic 2.1: Self- Awareness in the Community
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Self- Awareness in the Community, part of Life Skills in Education in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is public self-awareness important? 2. How can I improve my public self- awareness?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Self- Awareness in the Community together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: Learners discuss the importance of public-image (mannerisms, expressive qualities and decisions)

and make presentations in class.

• Creativity: Learners write articles on different personalities in society depicting how their public image has worked

for them and present in class.

18

Values:
● Respect: Learners tell stories about themselves to their classmates, then respectively receive feedback about their

public image.

● Love: Learners critique (with guidance) selected personalities’ public image against their perceived effectiveness in

their roles.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: Learners share their perceived public image with friends in class and how they can possibly enhance

it.

Suggested learning resources:

Digital devices with assistive technology, appropriate audio-visual clips, braille reference materials, print reference

materials with appropriate font and colour contrast, print and braille learner’s books, braille and print writing materials.
